title: Where things are
description: Say where something is, and where it is not.

explanation.summary: Estar is the verb for position, and it is irregular in the same way ser is. The forms are the ones you need on the first day: estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están.

sections.heading: The forms
sections.body: Only the yo form is regular: estoy. The rest change: estás, está, estamos, estáis, están. You can use estar with an adjective, with a place, and with a state: la puerta está cerrada, la casa está en la calle, estoy cansado.

examples.es: El libro está en la mesa.
examples.en: The book is on the table.

sections.heading: Ser and estar, side by side
sections.body: The difference is between what a thing is and how it is now. El café está frío means the coffee has gone cold. El café es frío means cold is what coffee is. Same for the place: estar is where it is, ser is what it is. The pair más and menos are for ser: es más grande, it is bigger. The pair muy and tan are for estar: está muy frío, it is very cold.

sections.heading: Saying where it is not
sections.body: Negatives put no in front: no está, no estoy. And there is a difference between not being somewhere and not doing something: no está en casa means it is not here, and no está trabajando means he is not working right now.

exercises.prompt: Pair each word with its translation.
exercises.note: Estar says where something is: la casa está cerca. The forms are irregular.
